title: Excelsior brass band and white and Black musicians working together
summary: George Moret's Excelsior band, Auburn Park engagements, mixed bands, and the great trumpeters Kimball, Oliver and Perez.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Who all was in the Excelsior band? Who was the leader?
Who was the leader? George Moret.
George Moret. Was it mostly on the other side of the river or over here? Did they play?

His brother was one of them, one of the great professors had that Moret's band. Yeah, I've heard of them. Up there in the city parks along. Auburn Park every year, every season. They had pregons and all that. You see, them days they had white and colored musicians worked together.

Sure, people worked with many of them. I hope to tell you. And all my twi in there, many of them. And one of our great trumpet players we had around here, the people in the city, didn't talk too much about it, but he was always working. You couldn't even tell you it was Andrew Kimball. One of the greatest reading trumpet and jazz trumpets. He was Andrew Kimball, Joe Oliver, and Mario Perez. That was the stiffest trumpet players they had around here. It says, buddy of bowling, stop. I mean stiff in musicals and jazz and you could hear from here to the river.
